r.정치 구도: South Sudan became independent from Sudan in 2011 after a referendum, but in 2013 the camps of the president and the vice president split and civil war broke out. Because the two sides drew support from the Dinka and the Nuer respectively, the fighting turned into an ethnic conflict, and hundreds of thousands of people are estimated to have died. A 2018 peace agreement brought both sides into a transitional unity government, but the merger of the armed forces and the drafting of a constitution lagged, and the transition has been extended several times. After an army base in Nasir in the north was attacked in March 2025, the opposition leader, then first vice president, was put under house arrest, and later that year he was charged with treason and murder and put on trial. The first national election since independence had been set for December 2026, but in November the electoral commission moved it to 11 February 2027. Most citizens have no identity documents, which slows voter registration, and the opposition objects to holding a vote while its leader is detained.

t.why: Landlocked South Sudan can only sell its oil by pumping it through pipelines across Sudan to Port Sudan on the Red Sea. Oil provides more than 90% of government revenue, so each time Sudan's civil war, which began in 2023, has shut the pipeline, the state's finances have been thrown into turmoil. When Sudan's Rapid Support Forces seized the Heglig oilfield, which the pipeline passes through, in December 2025, South Sudan reached a deal with both of Sudan's warring sides and moved its own troops in. Both countries claim the border area of Abyei, which is still guarded by UN troops. The UN Mission in South Sudan has been keeping the peace since independence, and with refugees arriving from Sudan's war, the country depends heavily on international humanitarian aid.
t.rel: It became independent from Sudan in 2011 but soon fell into civil war. It remains entangled with Sudan over the oil pipeline and the border area of Abyei.
t.korea: South Korea established diplomatic relations with South Sudan on 9 July 2011, the day it became independent. Around then the UN Secretary-General asked South Korea to send peacekeepers, and in March 2013 the Hanbit Unit, about 280 troops built around engineers, set up base in Bor in Jonglei state. The unit has mainly built roads and bridges, including a road that local people call the Road of Hope. It also runs vocational training and provides medical care. In 2026 it completed the UN's first smart camp at its Bor base.
t.know: Independent since 2011, South Sudan is the youngest member of the UN.
etext: At independence about three-quarters of the former Sudan's oil output came from South Sudan's territory. But the processing facilities and the export port are all in Sudan, so its oil can only be sold by paying fees to ship it through Sudan.
The White Nile runs through the middle of the country and fertile land is plentiful. But war and floods have kept farming from taking off, and a large share of food comes from imports and aid.

Apart from oil it has almost nothing to export, so when the pipeline stops, civil servants go months without pay. The currency has lost much of its value, prices have soared, and there are very few paved roads.
